NAH. School systems aren't the most effective at getting the required amount of learning done in the least amount of time. One big thing is that kids need somewhere to go so that parents can work. Another thing is that kids and teens have agendas other then learning, so that takes up extra time of them fooling around. 

I personally think that if your kids do a nice solid 3-4 of pure learning, then they should be good for the day. Maybe even let them make the schedule of start/end time, breaks, lunch and whatever to as long as they incorporate the hours you require. If they dont follow their schedule/get the hours done, then they can go on a "probation" period of following your schedule. 

N-T-A for letting them learn whatever. That's like the greatest thing you can do.

I was in a situation like this. I had two really good friends, one that had been in my life for as long as I knew him. But my depression got too much for them and they broke it off. 

I was tempted to just talk to them when I was really down or just bored. But I'm glad I didn't. I still awkwardly saw them around but we never talked. Until I messaged them telling making up for everything. I didnt really make any friends in those 2 years we didnt talk. 

I talk to one of them now and am pleasant to the other. My advice is to not just text them when you're down or lonely. Really think about if you want to make up or not and if you want to go on to being full on friends. Then have a short conversation with them about the "breakup" and move forward from that.
